title: Repositioning
text: A long day repositioning from Maine Yacht Center, Portland to Salem, MA. We were off the dock by 0430 and motoring through dense fog until it broke about 1000.  Got to try the new code sail for a bit and mixed the day up with some sailing and motor sailing.  The winds were all over the place but always on our bow.  Glad to be back on the home mooring.

title: Sea trials
text: Out and back and around Salem, Manchester, and Marblehead. We spent a while in 25-32kt winds running the new jib through its paces, tuning the inner forestay and runners to match.  It’s a really nice upgrade from the excellent but blown out North 3Di. It’s got a higher clew which is great for seeing lobster pots and broader shoulders giving us a lot of options with car position.

title: Pen Bay transit
text: Mostly motoring with almost no wind transiting Pen Bay through the middle of North Haven and Vinalhaven. Cold but sunny and enoug pots that I'm really ready for a break from northern new england.  Free mooring at Safe Harbor Rockland, the cleanest and friendliest place in Maine (alright Hinckley is tied for first).

title: Overnight to Somes Sound, MDI
text: Overnight run to MDI.  It was a nice overnight broad reach but died at sunrise once Cadillac and pots came into view

title: Pen Bay to home
text: Rough passage.  It was left over rollers that really threw us all over the boat.  Without much wind we were just motor sailing back to Cape Ann for sunrise and there was really no sleep for either of us. The commercial shipping lanes in and out of Portland and Porthsmouth were strangely busy so lots to monitor on AIS and radar. One of the funniest exchanges on VHF was recorded for those looking for the ultimate North Shore accent.  We arrive late morning to our mooring and after to relax a bit before driving home.  We were both weaving while walking for the next 24 hours.

title: Marella and friends
text: Marella, Michelle, and Nina got to enjoy the sun and Doug got to have a relaxing sail around Salem Harbor.

title: Salem to Provincetown and a whale
text: Got a 0745 start and a cold but wicked fast day sailing to P-Town.  We made a steady 8.5kts on a broad reach carrying the full main and code in 14-16 kites.  The waves picked up as we got closer to the destination making sure we were swing a lot once we got to the anchorage.  The Spade anchor set the second it hit the bottom but with quits overnight we left 5:1 including the snubber.  The exciting part is we nearly hit a right wale (we have video to prove) and I het to divert course and lay on the horn to avoid a collision.

title: PTown to Sandwich
text: Pretty quiet day across Cape Cod bay to time the channel pretty well.  We topped off on fuel at $5.99 a gallon (40 gallons) and got 1.2 gallons of gas in the jerry can for the dinghy. The slips in Sandwich are always crazy tight but this worked out fine.  Marella and I ate at Seafood Sam's for dinner at the recommendation of the fuel dock manager.  It was a good call but really rich.  Too many beers might have been the problem too, who knows. I ordered a new macerator pump before our trip South because no head would be a bad thing.

title: Edgartown to Cuttyhunk
text: Cool, sunny, and current filled day of sailign when we could and motoring the rest.  We needed to get to Cuttyhunk in time to get in a hike and stretch legs before nighfall. It was a fun location - smalled town by population in Massachusetts.  Saw it all in 45 minutes. Moorings were tight but people were nice and there is a raw bar that you can hail on channel 71 who will rock up with fresh seafood.

title: Sandwich to Edgartown
text: A reasonable 8am start from Sandwich to time the canal right.  We ended up going down Buzzards Bay under jib so as not to get to Wood's Hole until the current switched and even then we had to sail about at the entrace for an hour or two.  We were hailed by Steve Ricci from Pouchy who had just come from Hadley Harbor which was not even a location I knew - better place to hang for the hour or night.  It was a white knuckle run though Broadway at Woods Hole but I've done it enough it was fine.  As soon as we were through we were hailed by another boat still back in Buzzards Bay looking for a PIREP on current conditions.  Honestly, and don't tell anyone, but Vineyard Sound is a lousy sailing location.  Shoals everywhere, silly currents and Steamship Authority vessels all over the place.  We managed to broad reach to the entrance of Edgartown and settle in to mooring 32.  Dang do I love Edgartown.

title: Cuttyhunk to Provincetown
text: Full on day.  We left the second we could see where we were going.  The engine was warming up and coffe ready by 0530 and we cast off by 0545.  A nauseating motor back out the narrow channel into Buzzards Bay and we absolutely rockets up Buzzards Bay on a broad reach making 9kts in 12-15 kts of wind under a full main and the code zero.  We hit the channel just as the current was building around 9am, flew through about 11kts SOG and popped out into Cape Cod Bay as the line of torrential rain let loose.  We were prepared but it was spicy.  The most amazing Furuno radar finally just got lost in a wall of water - 3" per hour.  Rather than anchor I got us a mooring at Provincetown Marina which was mostly for peace of mind.  They were very nice but Marella and I never left the saloon choosing instead to sip a cocktail and play (learning) cribbage.
